paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility. It is characterized by defective oocyte maturation, with oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration. Impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and failed superovulation have also been reported (Yang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021; Du et al., 2023).

checks.claim: OZEMA29 is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TBPL2 was identified in two unrelated families characterized by oocyte maturation defects.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance can be inferred from homozygosity in infertile women, but the abstract does not state the inheritance pattern.

checks.evidence_quote: TBPL2 mutation might be associated with female infertility due to oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration

Her basal hormone levels were roughly normal, but her basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level was elevated. Her anti-Mullerian hormone level was within the normal range. paragraphs.text: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) studied Finnish women in the FinnGen cohort. Women homozygous for the TBPL2 R299X variant had an average of 0.16 (SD = 0.58) offspring, compared with 1.75 in the other genotype groups. According to registry data, only 4 women homozygous for the variant had children: of 41 homozygous individuals, 2 had given birth to 1 child and 2 had given birth to more than 1 child. All 4 had received infertility treatment, including IVF. In a phenome-wide analysis, the variant was associated only with infertility.

paragraphs.text: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) performed a genomewide association study of 22,849 Finnish women with infertility and 198,989 control women from FinnGen. Under a recessive model, they found a genomewide-significant association with a nonsense variant in the TBPL2 gene (c.895A-T, R299X; NM_199047.3), with an odds ratio of 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)). The variant introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of TBPL2. It was predicted with high confidence to be a loss-of-function variant (CADD score 40), and the authors expected it to significantly impair transcription of downstream targets.

checks.evidence_quote: is a rare stop-gained mutation (p.Arg299Ter, minor-allele frequency [MAF]: 1.1% in Finland) that is highly enriched to Finland (43 times compared to non-Finnish Europeans)
